title: Working Memory Optimisation
intro: Working Memory Optimisation examines how external memory support, AI summarisation and retrieval cues might improve working-memory performance without reducing independent recall.
lesson: For fifteen years, Jacob had been the person everyone relied on. Then the factory filled with dashboards, alerts and AI summaries. Information became abundant while confidence in remembering it began to thin. The Atlas research question is deliberately narrower than the story: which combinations of external memory support, AI summarisation and retrieval cues improve working-memory performance without reducing independent recall? The working hypothesis is that context-aware cueing at task boundaries may improve multi-step accuracy more than continuous summarisation while preserving unaided recall. The proposed evaluation combines controlled task experiments, repeated measures, interaction telemetry, interviews, subgroup analysis, delayed retention, adverse-effect capture and handback/recovery testing. The intended outcome is not simply faster output; it is useful assistance while retaining human capability.
